ideas: Leadership skills can be learned through practice
Some personality traits give people a head start
Examples of people who grew into leaders

phrases.meaning: become good at a job gradually

model: I disagree. I think leaders are mostly made, not born. First, most leadership skills, like communicating clearly or making decisions, come from hands-on experience. My current team leader is a good example. She's someone who was really quiet when she joined, but when our manager left suddenly, she had to step up and take charge. At first she struggled, but she's clearly grown into the role, and now she's running meetings with real confidence. Another reason is that leaders need to earn the trust of their team, and that comes from years of behaviour, not personality. A manager who keeps promises and treats people fairly will usually be respected, even if they're not very charismatic. I'm seeing this in my own job too; I'm leading a small project for the first time, and I'm learning something every week. Of course, some people are natural leaders, and confidence might give them a head start. But I believe anyone can rise to the occasion with practice, so for me, leaders are definitely made.
